answer: Newcomers must anchor a stake to one entry in a public atlas of live service endpoints. Each identity earns a plume: a trail of uptime proofs its endpoint alone can produce, since one endpoint cannot answer simultaneous live challenges for two identities. Auditors sample the atlas; a clone caught reusing an endpoint loses its anchor stake and its operator's other entries are frozen for inspection. Running n clones needs n live endpoints plus n stakes, and each extra endpoint raises the chance all are sampled together, so attacker cost grows faster than n times one honest identity.
